 Cable thefts cost Selangor flood facilities RM1.5mil
 By CY LEE 
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 | 6:54 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark

 Photo: KK SHAM/The Star 
 THEFT of cables and equipment at flood mitigation facilities has cost Selangor about RM1.5mil since 2023, affecting critical pumps and water gates in four districts.
 State infrastructure and agriculture committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim (pic) said 38 cases were recorded involving 33 pump houses and five water gates maintained by the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID).
 Klang recorded the highest losses at RM667,000 from eight cases, followed by Kuala Langat (RM499,000 from 17 cases), Kuala Selangor (RM318,000 from 10 cases) and Sepang (RM47,000 from three cases).
 Izham said the thefts not only caused financial losses but also disrupted the operation of flood mitigation facilities.
 “Sometimes, when the pumps are needed, we find that even the pump motors have been stolen,” he said during the Selangor State Assembly sitting at Bangunan Dewan Negeri Selangor in Shah Alam today (Nov 19).
 He was responding to Jefri Mejan (PN-Ijok), who asked about cable theft involving the Public Works Department (JKR) and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) since 2023, including losses and preventive measures.
 Izham said TNB had recorded 439 asset theft cases involving RM62.7mil in losses between January 2023 and September 2026.
 Of these, 166 cases were recorded in the first nine months of this year, with Cheras accounting for 45 cases, Bangi (37) and Pelabuhan Klang (24).
 For JKR, he said official records were unavailable, although losses were estimated at between RM50,000 and RM100,000 per incident.
 In a supplementary question, Jefri raised concerns about cable theft affecting street lighting along FT54 (Kepong-Kuala Selangor) and B35 (Bukit Badong-Bestari Jaya), which he said endangered motorists.
 He asked whether funds were available to repair the affected streetlights before the end of 2026.
 Izham said he had asked JKR and relevant agencies to progressively replace conventional streetlights with integrated solar LED systems to reduce cable theft.
 However, he did not have specific information on repairs for the two roads.
 He said efforts to combat cable theft should also target syndicates buying stolen cables, adding that he had discussed the problem with the Selangor police chief.
 “We should not just look at thefts after they occur.
 “We also need to identify the syndicates buying these stolen cables,” he said.
 Other preventive measures include increased patrols, installing anti-climb fencing and stronger locks, and deploying closed-circuit television (CCTV) monitoring at vulnerable sites.
 Azmizam Zaman Huri (PH-Pelabuhan Klang) also proposed involving residents in monitoring cable theft through a community programme supported by incentives.
 Izham said the state would consider additional measures to strengthen security at vulnerable infrastructure sites.
